fact: On 2026-09-03 Kenya launched an official guide to investigating and prosecuting 76 listed cyber offences under the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act, presented by the Internal Security PS as the common operational framework under that Act.

The report says two false-publication sections of Kenya's Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act were struck down by the Court of Appeal, and that a 2025 amendment to the Act was partly struck down in a later challenge, so the Act otherwise stands; published 2026-07-28, no event date given.

The report says Kenya's existing cybersecurity framework rests on the National Computer and Cybercrimes Coordination Committee under the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act, to which the new National Cybersecurity Agency (Legal Notice 89 of 2026) adds capacity; published 2026-09-11, no other date given.
The article says the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act has been put in place to address risks on digital platforms; no event date is given, so the published date 2026-09-08 is used.

The Nation reports the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act establishes a coordination committee and was amended by the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes (Amendment) Act, 2024, widening investigators' and courts' powers; no event date beyond the published date 2026-06-22 is used.
The Southern Africa Litigation Centre says Kenya's Court of Appeal struck down two sections of the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act in March 2026, leaving the rest of the Act in place.

The Daily Nation reports the Court of Appeal struck down sections 22 and 23 of the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act, 2018, but upheld sections 16, 17, 27, 28, 37 and investigative powers under sections 48 to 53, so the Act stands.

The Daily Nation says dozens of young social media users have faced arrests and prosecutions under the Act, increasing after the June 2024 protests, including teacher Albert Ojwang, arrested over a social media post and who died in custody in June 2025.
Kenya's Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes (Amendment) Act, 2025 (No. 17 of 2025), assented 15 October 2025 and commencing 4 November 2025, amends the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act, Cap. 79C.

Parliament of Kenya says the National Assembly passed the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes (Amendment) Bill, 2024, with amendments.
CPJ says Kenya's 2018 Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act took effect after a 2020 High Court ruling, with October amendments giving a national cybercrime committee power to ban sites and apps.
Journalist Peter Mwita was charged in a Mombasa court under the cybercrimes law over a WhatsApp message and pleaded not guilty; CPJ lists other bloggers and journalists arrested under it.
The Star reports NC4 was established under the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act of 2018, and that President Ruto assented to an amended Cybercrimes Act on 15 October 2025.

CIPESA states the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act was enacted in 2018 and criminalises certain online expression including false publications, with the Court of Appeal in March 2026 leaving its investigative powers largely intact.
